blocks.intent: Prove that a group homomorphism preserves the identity.

attempts.candidate: thm homomorphism_maps_identity using f(one_A * one_A), target right identity, and left cancellation
attempts.diagnosis: Multiplication preservation turns idempotence of the source identity into a cancellable equality in the target.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm homomorphism_maps_identity:
    ? forall [GroupHomomorphismSetting]:
        f(one_A) = one_B
    mul_A(one_A, one_A) = one_A
    f(mul_A(one_A, one_A)) = mul_B(f(one_A), f(one_A))
    by thm group_mul_one(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f(one_A))
    mul_B(f(one_A), f(one_A)) = f(mul_A(one_A, one_A)) = f(one_A) = mul_B(f(one_A), one_B)
    by thm group_left_cancel(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f(one_A), f(one_A), one_B)
blocks.reusable_lesson: Identity preservation needs only multiplication preservation plus target-group cancellation.

blocks.intent: Prove the tracer theorem that a group homomorphism preserves inverses.

attempts.candidate: thm homomorphism_maps_inverse by turning f(inv_A(a)) into f(inv_A(a)) * (f(a) * inv_B(f(a))) and reassociating
attempts.diagnosis: The source left-inverse law maps to a target left inverse; target right identity and right inverse identify it with inv_B(f(a)).
attempts.next_change: Materialize the accepted source prefix and run the file gate.

blocks.accepted_litex:
thm homomorphism_maps_inverse:
    ? forall [GroupHomomorphismSetting], a A:
        f(inv_A(a)) = inv_B(f(a))
    by thm homomorphism_maps_identity(A, B, mul_A, one_A, inv_A, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f)
    mul_A(inv_A(a), a) = one_A
    f(mul_A(inv_A(a), a)) = mul_B(f(inv_A(a)), f(a))
    mul_B(f(inv_A(a)), f(a)) = f(mul_A(inv_A(a), a)) = f(one_A) = one_B
    by thm group_mul_one(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f(inv_A(a)))
    by thm group_mul_inv(B, mul_B, one_B, inv_B, f(a))
    f(inv_A(a)) = mul_B(f(inv_A(a)), one_B) = mul_B(f(inv_A(a)), mul_B(f(a), inv_B(f(a)))) = mul_B(mul_B(f(inv_A(a)), f(a)), inv_B(f(a))) = mul_B(one_B, inv_B(f(a))) = inv_B(f(a))
blocks.reusable_lesson: Inverse preservation is clearest as a uniqueness-of-inverse calculation; no custom inverse predicate is needed.
